Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.

Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.
Replace @root_validator with @model_validator; pre=True becomes mode='before' on a classmethod taking the raw dict, otherwise mode='after' on an instance method returning self.
Replace @root_validator with @model_validator(mode='before') on a classmethod that works on the input dict.

Remove Config.json_encoders; add @field_serializer for the affected fields (or a PlainSerializer in Annotated) that produces the same output, and move other Config keys to model_config = ConfigDict(...).
Remove json_encoders and add a @model_serializer(mode='wrap') that formats datetimes the same way.
Turn the __root__ model into a pydantic.RootModel[...] subclass and use .root instead of .__root__; parse with model_validate.
Replace the __root__ model with a TypeAdapter over the inner type plus a plain helper class.
Replace Model.update_forward_refs() with Model.model_rebuild().

Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod; pre=True becomes mode='before', each_item=True becomes validating the list items in the function, always=True becomes validate_default=True on the Field.
Move the check into an Annotated type with AfterValidator / BeforeValidator.
Replace @validate_arguments with @validate_call.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod, take info: ValidationInfo and read earlier fields from info.data instead of values.
Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.

Replace `PostCode.__get_validators__` with `__get_pydantic_core_schema__(cls, source_type, handler)` returning `core_schema.no_info_plain_validator_function(cls.validate)`. Import `core_schema` from `pydantic_core`; this keeps the existing normalization and validation logic while removing the deprecated hook.

Replace the `PostCode` subclass and its `__get_validators__` hook with an `Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(...)]` alias. Have the before-validator convert the input to a string, remove spaces, uppercase it, check for exactly five digits, and return the normalized string; keep `Delivery.post_code` annotated as `PostCode`.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model.model_validate(data).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate_json(body).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate(json.loads(body)).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model.model_validate(data).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.schema() with Model.model_json_schema().
Replace .copy(update=...) with .model_copy(update=...).
Replace .copy(update=...) with Model(**{**obj.model_dump(), **update}).
Replace Model.__fields__ with Model.model_fields; field.required becomes field.is_required(), outer_type_ becomes annotation.
Set model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True) and replace Model.from_orm(obj) with Model.model_validate(obj).
Replace Model.construct(**data) with Model.model_construct(**data).
Replace .dict(...) with .model_dump(...), keeping the same keyword arguments.
Replace .dict() with dict(obj) and filter keys by hand.
Import Field from pydantic and declare key as Union[int, str] = Field(union_mode="left_to_right"); this makes Pydantic try int first, converting "42" to 42 while still accepting nonnumeric strings.
Add a @field_validator("key", mode="before") that converts string values accepted by int() to integers and returns other strings unchanged; import field_validator from pydantic.
Import `field_validator` from Pydantic and add a `@field_validator("sku", mode="before")` that returns `str(value)` for integer inputs, allowing numeric SKUs to validate as strings.
Define `sku` as `Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(str)]` (importing `Annotated` and `BeforeValidator`) so input values are converted to strings before Pydantic validates the field.
In from_sensor, pass int(reading) as units when constructing StockLevel so fractional sensor readings are truncated before integer validation.
Add a @field_validator('units', mode='before') to StockLevel that converts numeric inputs to int, truncating fractional readings before Pydantic validates the integer field.
Replace the `parse_obj_as` import and call with `TypeAdapter`: import `TypeAdapter` from `pydantic`, then return `TypeAdapter(list[User]).validate_python(rows)` from `load_users`.
Remove the `parse_obj_as` import and replace its use with `[User.model_validate(row) for row in rows]`, returning the validated users as a list.

In changed_fields, replace the deprecated __fields_set__ access with model_fields_set: return sorted(ProfilePatch(**raw).model_fields_set).

In changed_fields, dump the validated model with exclude_unset=True and return its keys: return sorted(ProfilePatch(**raw).model_dump(exclude_unset=True).keys()). This preserves explicitly supplied fields, including fields set to None, without using the deprecated attribute.
Add a Pydantic v2 `@field_serializer("price")` method to `Quote` that returns `float(value)`. Then `model_dump(mode="json")` encodes the price as a JSON number.
Change `publish` to call `json.dumps(q.model_dump(mode="python"), default=float)`, so the `Decimal` price is converted to a float and emitted as a JSON number.

Import `field_serializer` from `pydantic` and add a JSON-only serializer to `Shift`: `@field_serializer("started", when_used="json")` returning `value.isoformat()`. This formats UTC offsets as `+00:00` instead of `Z`.

Define an annotated datetime type using `Annotated[datetime, PlainSerializer(lambda value: value.isoformat(), return_type=str, when_used="json")]`, importing `Annotated` and `PlainSerializer`, and use that type for `Shift.started`. Its JSON serialization will preserve the `+00:00` offset.

Change `at` to type `date`, import `date` and `field_validator`, and add a `@field_validator("at", mode="before")` that converts incoming `datetime` values to `value.date()`. This makes the field date-only and encodes it as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
